subject: Re: Escape Ladder — Pricing Anchoring and Order Form Redlines
messages:
From: Jaya Patel <jaya.patel@acme.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Systems Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form — escape ladder / pricing anchoring concern

David —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we take the draft order form back to our procurement & legal teams theres one structural concern that keeps coming up: the "escape ladder" language in Exhibit B (pricing anchoring). At a high level Acme is worried that the escape ladder allows rapid step-ups in unit pricing if our usage dips relative to forecast, and the admin-triggered re-anchoring could create a significant short-term cost spike while our teams stabilize adoption.

Specific asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a firm definition of the trigger and a cap on the per-token step increase?
- Can we build a short-term billing holdback / smoothing mechanism (60–90 days) while usage normalizes?
- We also want an explicit true-up cadence and a right to dispute any re-anchor within 30 days of notice.

If you could send a proposed redline for Exhibit B and the order schedule with those elements included that would help speed review on our end. Were aiming to finalize commercial terms this month.

Appreciate it —
Jaya
Jaya Patel
Sr. Manager, Procurement — Acme Systems

Team — forwarding Acme's note. TL;DR: they want stricter guardrails around the escape-ladder (trigger definition, per-token cap, short smoothing/holdback, dispute window). Theyre motivated to close this month, so let's be practical here.

Legal / Pricing asks:
- Marissa: can you produce a redline for Exhibit B that adds a quantifiable step cap (absolute $ or % per step) and an explicit 60–90 day smoothing/holdback for step increases? Also include a 30-day dispute right and a 6-month maximum re-anchor frequency.
- Ben/Laura: does this align with our revenue recognition / billing ops? Any operational constraints if we add a holdback and 90-day smoothing? If so, propose alternatives.

I attached the draft order form we sent earlier for context. If possible please get a candidate redline back to me by EOD tomorrow so I can push to Acme.

Attachments: draft_orderform_v2.pdf

Thanks,
David

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Aug 2025 18:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order form — escape ladder / pricing anchoring concern

David / all —

Attached is a proposed legal redline for Exhibit B (OrderForm_Escalator_Redline.docx). High-level summary of the changes I inserted:

1) Trigger definition: the re-anchor trigger is now defined as a 30-day rolling average drop below 60% of the committed monthly usage (previous language was subjective). The re-anchor notice must include the usage data and calculations.

2) Step cap: each step-up in the escape ladder is capped at either $0.0025 per unit or 7% of the then-current per-unit price, whichever is lower. This prevents outsized instantaneous increases.

3) Smoothing / holdback: new 60-day smoothing period for any step-up where the billed rate increases are applied incrementally over two equal invoiced periods (30 days each). Additionally, Redwood will escrow the first 40% of incremental charges (holdback) collected during the smoothing window pending the 90-day post-re-anchor reconciliation. If the re-anchor is later found to be incorrect, holdback will be returned as a credit.

4) Dispute and cadence: Customer has 30 days from notice to dispute; Redwood will not collect disputed amounts until dispute resolution. Re-anchor frequency limited to once per 180 days unless both parties agree otherwise.

5) Operational note: Ben / Laura, I added a clause requiring Redwood to provide a reconciliation report and the raw usage dataset in CSV within 10 business days of notice. That should make disputes less noisy.

I kept the language narrow to limit downstream accounting headaches but gave the customer the protections they asked for. If Ben flags material billing issues I can tighten the escrow percentage or extend the smoothing window to 90 days instead.

Attaching: OrderForm_Escalator_Redline.docx (track changes), Pricing_Matrix_v3.xlsx (example showing cap math).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jaya Patel <jaya.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form — escape ladder / pricing anchoring concern

Jaya —

Thanks for the clear ask. Weve reviewed and propose the attached redline to Exhibit B that reflects the protections you requested. Summary of the compromise (high level):
- Defined a 30-day rolling average trigger and required Redwood to provide the usage dataset and calculations with any re-anchor notice.
- Capped each step increase at the lower of $0.0025 per token or 7% of the then-current per-token charge.
- Implemented a 60-day smoothing window (two billing periods) and an escrow/holdback of 40% of incremental charges during the smoothing period, refundable after a 90-day reconciliation if the re-anchor is reversed.
- 30-day dispute window and re-anchor frequency capped at once per 180 days.

We believe this balances Acme's need for predictability with Redwoods need to protect unit economics for genuine usage declines. I attached the tracked redline and a pricing matrix that shows example math for a 3-step ladder at different volumes.

If that framework looks acceptable in principle we can produce a final order form for signature and a DocuSign packet. Marissa: if youre comfortable with the language Ill share the DocuSign link and loop our finance ops for billing setup.

Attachments: OrderForm_Escalator_Redline.docx, Pricing_Matrix_v3.xlsx, Acme_MutualActionPlan.pdf

Best,
David Kim
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

David —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the concrete language. The step cap + smoothing are acceptable in principle. A couple of quick follow-ups from Acme legal:
- Please add an explicit example in Exhibit B that shows the math for a 3-step ladder and the escrow calculation for transparency.
- We'd like the dispute resolution timeline to reference Redwoods reconciliation report (i.e., Customer can submit a dispute plus the reconciliation report will be the primary evidence).

If you can add that example and the reconciliation reference well route for signature. Also please send the DocuSign packet once the final redline is in.

Thanks — were close.
Jaya
Sr. Manager, Procurement — Acme Systems
